Eleven takeaways from the NATO Summit in Ankara

status_summary: At the Hague Summit on 2025-06-25, NATO Allies committed to spend 5% of GDP annually on defence by 2035, with at least 3.5% for core defence requirements and up to 1.5% for broader defence and security investment, annual plans showing a credible path, and a review in 2029. NATO's spending page, last updated 2026-06-29, reports that European Allies and Canada together reached 2.3% of GDP in 2025, up from 1.4% in 2014, with nearly 20% real growth over 2024. Press and analysis coverage of the Ankara Summit (held 2026-07-07 and 2026-07-08) reports that President Trump pressed allies on the 5% goal, that the declaration reaffirmed Article 5, and that Spain is the only member that has not pledged to reach the target; a wire report dated 2026-07-08 says NATO Secretary General Rutte credited Trump with pressing allies to spend more. The commitment exceeds the 2 percent pledge the Mandate named, but actual spending by most Allies remains below the new target and the specific US negotiating steps are not documented in the sources found.

timeline.event: NATO's Hague Summit Declaration commits Allies to invest 5% of GDP annually by 2035 (at least 3.5% on core defence and up to 1.5% on defence- and security-related spending), requires annual plans showing a credible path, and sets a review of the trajectory in 2029.

NATO's defence expenditure page (last updated this date) reports 2025 data: European Allies and Canada raised spending by nearly 20% in real terms over 2024 and reached 2.3% of GDP combined, compared with 1.4% in 2014.

Washington Examiner reports that President Trump is heading to the Ankara summit expected to press allies to spend at least 5% of GDP on defense; the headline says he is weighing penalties for allies that fall short, though the article text gives no specifics.

NATO's Ankara summit concludes with a short declaration (summit held 2026-07-07 and 2026-07-08). An Atlantic Council analysis published 2026-07-09 reports the declaration reaffirmed Article 5, cites progress toward the 5% goal, names Spain as reluctant, and notes friction between Washington and allies over spending, troop levels, Iran and Greenland.

A wire report from the end of the Ankara summit says NATO Secretary General Rutte credited President Trump with pressing allies to spend more, Trump said some allies have fully responded and others are making major changes, and Spain is the only member that has not pledged to reach the 5% goal.

title: Press NATO allies to meet and exceed the 2 percent defense spending pledge
uncertainties: The NATO pages show the allied commitment and spending trend; a wire report attributes to Secretary General Rutte the view that Trump's pressure drove added spending, but the US negotiating steps toward the Hague target are not documented, and the link between US pressure and the outcome rests on that attribution. The Washington Examiner article's visible text gave no detail on the penalties named in its headline. The NATO pages did not report per-Ally figures, and the Atlantic Council piece is analysis by outside authors; its 2.53 percent European and Canadian average is a different, more recent figure than NATO's 2.3 percent for 2025. No US executive order, State Department action or legislation on NATO burden-sharing was searched in the Federal Register.
